html.content:
Recommended

Spaghettiscore: 1.0

Individual trajectory lines per subject over time.

Clinical use: Individual patient lab trajectories, PK per-subject profiles

  • moderate n — trajectories readable

generate_canvasxpress_config with description='spaghetti plot of <numeric> over <time> per <subject_id>'

This chart type is ideal for visualizing

Alternatives

Dotplotscore: 1.0

Individual data points per group — best when n < ~50 per group.

Clinical use: Individual lab values, small Phase I cohorts

  • cat + numeric
  • medium n — dotplot still viable

generate_canvasxpress_config with description='dot plot of <numeric> by <factor>'

Linescore: 1.0

Connected points showing trends over a continuous or ordinal axis.

Clinical use: Lab values over visits, PK concentration-time profiles

  • colour by category
  • enough time points

generate_canvasxpress_config with description='line chart of <numeric> over <time> colored by <factor>'

Barscore: 0.85

Vertical or horizontal bars comparing values across categories.

Clinical use: AE counts by SOC/arm, subject counts by group

  • 1+ category + 1+ numeric
  • small-medium dataset

generate_canvasxpress_config with description='grouped bar chart of <metric> by <category>'

Treemapscore: 0.85

Nested rectangles sized by value — hierarchical proportion.

Clinical use: Hierarchical AE counts (SOC → PT)

  • cat + numeric → hierarchical size
  • nested hierarchy
  • many categories → treemap handles well

generate_canvasxpress_config with description='treemap of <numeric> by <factor> hierarchy'
